Added DualSense controller detection through Steam Input, with PlayStation button prompts, including corrected Help/Close symbols.

Improved vessel falling behaviour when airborne.
Improved job-menu scrolling, controller prompts and button layout. Contract titles and destinations are now more consistent across job offers, the quest log and calendar.

Following our Open Beta testing phase, we're happy to release Patch 1.1, bringing a range of gameplay improvements, bug fixes, and quality-of-life adjustments.

This update focuses on improving mission progression, ship handling, multiplayer functionality, and overall game stability. It also introduces new features and usability improvements, including harbour fast travel, updated trading mechanics, and additional player guidance.
We've also addressed several additional issues identified during the Open Beta, including crashes, ship handling problems, and cargo-related bugs.
Added harbour fast travel buttons.
Disabled fast travel within harbour areas.
Adjusted resource consumption and restrictions.
Added several tutorial cards for improved player guidance.
Integrated campaign bonuses into regular mission rewards. Single-shift jobs no longer offer a separate claimable bonus.
Improved camera function of the binocular.
Updated harbour icons in Quickplay and on the navigation map for smaller harbours.
Updated achievement/trophy descriptions.
Improved pacing and player guidance in campaign chapters 1, 2, and 6.
Fixed missing, duplicate, or misleading markers across several missions.
Added world markers for ship transfers.
Added harbourmaster tasks to transport missions and corrected several harbourmaster interactions.
Fixed an issue in "My Career" where loaded LNG and bulk cargo could be lost when switching ships.
Adjusted handling for Bernhard, Density, and Lancer to reduce overly sharp turns.

Adjusted harbour trading balance and added dynamic trade price calculations.

Fixed missing escort markers, inspection information, and warning sounds for multiplayer clients.
Improved binocular visibility and animation synchronisation.
Enabled ship light controls for multiplayer clients.
Improved player list updates and world marker synchronisation.
Fixed crashes when switching ships during trading.
Fixed an issue when travelling to different spawn points on the Nordic Duchess.
Fixed various additional crashes to improve overall stability.
Improved calendar readability, map labels, mission text, and harbour travel buttons.
Fixed HUD display issues related to speed indicators and spacing on several ships.
Fixed persistent “new” indicators and recurring unlock notifications.
Improved ship models, harbour scenery, glass materials, nighttime window lighting, hair, and character animations.
Improved rain, LNG, crane, footstep, horn, sonar, and mission audio.
Added a potential fix for an issue where water could disappear when wind speed reached zero.
Updated translations, tutorial text, dialogue, and error messages across several supported languages.
Made additional localisation adjustments.

Multiplayer clients may not receive rewards after completing a mission.

We hope you enjoy Patch 1.1!

Early Access Update 5: The Co-op Crew Update is now live on the default branch!
A huge thank you to everyone who joined us on the public_beta branch, tested the update early, reported issues, and shared their feedback with us.

The main focus of the Co-op Crew Update is multiplayer. For the first time, you can form a crew with up to three other players and operate the same vessel together across selected cargo operations, firefighting missions, rescue missions, and more.

Alongside multiplayer, the update introduces two new missions, expands the Free Trade system with LNG and bulk cargo, and includes several improvements addressing feedback and issues from the Career Update.
Before we get into everything included in the update, take a look at the release trailer:
[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45525680/354020d4aa8024f7de07ffd7b2c5447494319c24.jpg"]
You can now create or join a multiplayer session with up to four players and operate the same vessel together.
Depending on the mission, you can divide responsibilities, complete different tasks at the same time, and support each other throughout the operation.

During container cargo operations with the Herbert, one player can operate the crane while another handles the twist locks and lashing rods. On the Big Trip, two players can control both cranes simultaneously and load or unload containers in parallel.

For LNG operations, one player can operate the crane while the rest of the crew manages the loading or unloading process. During bulk cargo missions, two players can operate the cranes at the same time.

Firefighting and rescue missions give larger crews even more ways to work together. One player can steer the vessel while up to three others operate the fire extinguishers, or support a rescue operation by throwing lifebuoys and assisting the pilot.
Cargo activities are especially well suited to crews of two, while firefighting and rescue missions allow crews of up to four players to contribute at the same time.
[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45525680/685023a80f17f6cc0d7f58a4cad23e16c855d039.jpg"]
The Co-op Crew Update also introduces two new missions.
Highjacked! is now available in Mettington after reaching Reputation Level 3 in the harbor and obtaining either the Rigid or the Density.
Exchange and Jump In! has been added to all major harbors and becomes available after obtaining a tugboat.

The Free Trade system has also been expanded with LNG and bulk cargo. Both cargo types can now be bought and sold between major harbors, giving you more options for building your career and making use of your vessels.
[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45525680/58d5cbad2aa9f52966f5f7517017c3035c0208e3.png"]
We’re happy to welcome Knabe Drinks by HandOfBlood into the world of Seafarer!
With its strong connection to the gaming community, the partnership feels like a great fit for Seafarer, and you’ll now be able to spot Knabe Drinks in-game as part of life aboard your vessels.
And if you’re visiting us at gamescom next week, keep an eye out – you might also get the chance to try a Knabe Mix at our booth. 🥤
We’re excited to have Knabe Drinks on board and to bring this collaboration into Seafarer! 🧡
[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45525680/df2b3913d26e792092752494a6f9d3e35a619cdb.jpg"]
The update also includes several improvements addressing feedback and issues from the Career Update.

Trading information is now clearer, cargo availability has been increased, and the harbor schedule and Reputation progression have been improved. Work Shifts, controller support, mission rewards, and several related systems have also received adjustments.
You can find the complete list of changes in the changelog below.
Multiplayer is now accessible! You can now play in a group of up to 4 players, completing curated missions together.
Knabe billboards in harbours
Containers featuring Knabe branding
A random delivery event featuring Knabe drinks
Several goods in the Free Trade system have had their prices adjusted to be more profitable.
Added several hints, pop-ups and warnings in missions.
Work Shifts now provide their payment after every completed shift instead of at the end of a mission.
Work Shifts can now be claimed at the end of a mission, providing additional Reputation for every manually completed shift.
Players can now repair, refill their resources and upgrade their ship equipment even on inactive vessels.
Campaign missions now grant Reputation.
Inspection missions now end with a results screen summarizing the vessel's status.
Highjacked! A new mission has been added in Mettington. It becomes available after reaching Reputation Level 3 in Mettington and obtaining a Rigid or Density.
Exchange and Jump In! A new mission has been added in all major harbours. It becomes available after obtaining a Tugboat.
LNG has been added to the Free Trade system and can now be traded freely between major harbours.
Bulk cargo has been added to the Free Trade system and can now be traded freely between major harbours.
Several bug fixes, including major issues reported by the community.
The following improvements were originally planned for Hot Fix #2 and are now included as part of Patch #5.0.
Cargo Compatibility
Issue: It was not clear which cargo types could be transported by which ships, causing unavailable trading options to be perceived as bugs.

Fix: Containers now have clear labels, and the ship menu displays which cargo types the selected vessel can transport. In addition, the trading screen now explains that certain goods can only be transported using the Big Trip.
Big Trip Trading Improvements
Issue: Trading could fail even when sufficient total cargo capacity was available if containers were not evenly distributed across both cargo sections.
Fix: The Big Trip now supports asymmetric cargo distribution between its cargo sections, allowing purchases to succeed as long as enough overall capacity is available.
Market Rotation Timer
Issue: Players could not see when a port's market inventory would refresh.
Fix: The trading screen now displays the remaining time until the next market rotation, along with an explanation that market offers refresh periodically.
Loading Service
Issue: Manually loading and unloading containers was time-consuming, and the feature was not clearly explained.

Fix: A paid loading service now automatically loads and unloads all compatible containers. The interface has also been improved with a clearer button and a confirmation dialog showing the associated costs.
Increased Cargo Availability
Issue: Trading opportunities were frequently limited by the number of available cargo containers.
Fix: The number of containers available for trading has been significantly increased, making goods available more frequently and in larger quantities.
New Trade Goods
Issue: Some container types were not available through the trading system.
Fix: Bulk and LNG cargo can now be bought and sold through the regular trading system.
Extended Harbour Schedule
Issue: The previous 7-day schedule provided limited visibility for planning future deliveries.
Fix: The harbour schedule has been expanded to four weeks. Deliveries are now highlighted more clearly, and individual days can be selected directly.
Skip to Selected Day
Issue: Players had to advance time step by step to reach future events.
Fix: Players can now skip directly to a selected day from the harbour schedule. A confirmation dialog is displayed before time is advanced.
Locked Harbour Information
Issue: Locked harbours did not indicate when or how they could be unlocked.
Fix: Locked harbours now display the required global reputation level needed for unlocking.
Controller Support
Issue: Not all new menus and features were fully accessible using a controller.
Fix: Controller support has been expanded to cover the new user interface and gameplay features.
Rebalanced Reputation Progression
Issue: Progression pacing for unlocking new content was uneven and could result in unnecessary delays.
Fix: Reputation requirements for harbour unlocks, missions, and player levels have been rebalanced to provide a smoother progression experience.
Campaign Reputation Rewards
Issue: Campaign missions only rewarded players indirectly through the work completed during the mission.
Fix: Campaign missions now grant additional direct reputation rewards, making campaign progression more rewarding.
Multiplayer

Clients will sometimes not see the actual containers on Ferries
Clients cannot interact with the ship horn
Reputation
There are currently no credits rewarded when the player increases their reputation
Missions
Currently a problem with the rewards calculation where some missions are giving much less credits and reputation than anticipated
Occasionally, while unloading the Big Trip in “Exchange and Jump in” the mission will automatically cancel itself
Practice Course currently does not grant any rewards
Bulk
The Bulk Hatch Screen cannot be opened via controller
The Bulk Hatch screen does not currently respond while undocked.
Miscellaneous
The digital clock currently does not work as intended.
After fast travel the sea map has to be closed manually
While interacting with icons in “Challenges” the icons might change their appearance

After its time in Open Beta, our fourth major Early Access Update is now available on the main branch.

First of all, thank you to everyone who jumped into the public_beta, tested the new systems, reported issues, and shared feedback with us. Your input gives us a clearer picture of what to keep improving as development continues throughout Early Access.

The Career Update is all about giving progression in Seafarer more structure and making your own ships feel more connected to your long-term journey. This update introduces the new My Career system, expands the campaign with new missions, replaces EXP with reputation, improves inspection gameplay, and adds new features to make your time at sea feel more varied.

For existing save games, this does not mean losing your progress. Existing levels will be transferred directly into the new reputation system, so if you’re at level 10, you will start at reputation level 10. Content that you’ve already unlocked or purchased will remain available. However, which contracts and opportunities are available may change as part of the new progression system.
Before we get into the details, check out the release trailer:
The next three campaign missions continue Teddy’s story and bring this chapter to its conclusion.

Without going into spoilers, you can expect new story moments, high-stakes situations, firefighting operations, and intense action at sea. These missions add more depth to Teddy’s journey and bring new dramatic moments to the world of Seafarer.
After completing the campaign, you can of course continue your sandbox career.
[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45525680/6a6224555d47cdd98e0bc8e6a3c0fe1142e72fe9.jpg"]
The Career Update introduces My Career, a major rework of the current gameplay structure.
Your own ships now play a bigger role in your personal progression. The new system creates a clearer difference between mission gameplay and your long-term career as an independent captain.

You can trade goods, make use of trading opportunities, and use your ships outside of classic missions. Instead of only waiting for a contract, you’ll have more freedom to observe ports, buy goods, store them, transport them, and sell them later for a profit.

For the start, this system focuses on container trading. It gives owned ships a stronger purpose and adds a new layer to the overall gameplay loop. Your ship becomes more of an investment, a useful tool, and a personal project that can grow over time. Also: no more random containers on your ships!
[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45525680/d34abaefe1ab6f0bb6550203d2ee4415f3fa52da.jpg"]

Some operations now also become longer-running workflows within the game world. Freighters can be loaded over several days, routes can be prepared, and transports can move through different stages. You can take part in these processes, but you do not always have to complete every step yourself.
The goal is to make it feel more like you are building your own career at sea. You get to choose!

The goal is to make it feel more like you are building your own career at sea. You get to choose!
[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45525680/1b84fa1880b96b780c41576fd7bd054f6d35baf9.jpg"]
The previous EXP system has been replaced with a new Reputation System.

You now earn reputation with individual harbors, unlocking new ships, missions, and opportunities as your standing grows. Local harbor reputation also contributes to your global reputation, which gradually opens up more of the world and replaces the previous player level system.
As your reputation grows, the world will begin to react to you differently, making progression feel more connected to what you do in the Seafarer world.
Inspection gameplay has been expanded into a deeper and more interactive experience.

Inspections now involve more steps and more ways to understand what is happening on board. You can check documents, inspect technical areas, speak with crew members, look into safety concerns, and gather information before completing the job.

This makes inspections feel more connected to the world and gives them a stronger role within the overall career experience. They are no longer just a quick task, but a more detailed activity that asks you to look closer, pay attention, and piece together the situation on the vessel.
[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45525680/2e7f9501d4fe55888a121805c9bf7233abc618a2.jpg"]
A new unlockable drone gives you another way to explore the world from above.

The drone can be used on almost all ships and provides a helpful new perspective for exploration and rescue missions. It is especially useful in rough weather, heavy seas, or situations where spotting shipwrecked people or points of interest from your vessel can be difficult.
The drone has a limited range and cannot be used in certain harbor areas due to no-fly zones, but it adds a new way to look around and take in the scale of the world.
Bulk ships now feature optional deck cleaning gameplay.
When loading bulk cargo, your ship’s deck can become visibly dirty from dust and cargo residue. You can clean it manually whenever you like, creating a calm maintenance activity between missions.
Deck cleaning is fully optional and mainly focused on immersion and atmosphere. It gives you another small way to take care of your ship and make it feel more like your own.
[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45525680/d6832163bbb9fe2cda552d92b4842ca6d539c0f6.jpg"]
With the Career Update, career progression, reputation, owned ships, inspections, and trading are now more closely connected.
Together, these changes give your own ships and your reputation a bigger role in how you progress through Seafarer.
The update also moves the game another step toward a broader maritime sandbox career, while still building on the existing mission-based structure.
Several of the features in this update are based on community feedback, especially around career progression, owned ships, inspections, and a more active sandbox world.

items.text: Early Access Update 3, the Immersion Update, is now live on the default branch!
Before we dive into the details, take a look at our release trailer:
[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45525680/5129d9dc1180dbab73f0985f58524b99b7d3683c.gif"]

With this update, Seafarer takes a strong step forward in how it feels to play. The Immersion Update focuses on making the world more alive, responsive, and engaging, while also expanding the campaign experience.
[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45525680/46f3dcc03c5776fd6ce3abac63ae0d505d9c1f8d.gif"]

Teddy has received a full overhaul, now appearing as a more rugged and experienced seafarer, complete with new voiceovers. He now adds more authenticity to our setting the newly reworked campaign, guiding you more naturally through your journey.

Missions 1 and 2 have been fully reworked with new animation sequences and improved storytelling, while Mission 3 continues the narrative with a brand-new chapter. Together, these changes significantly enhance the flow and presentation of Seafarer’s story.
[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45525680/085c3ef9fd34d8b21c20926fdd7c9eb60b998e1b.gif"]

Beyond the campaign, new systems deepen the overall experience. Inspection gameplay has been expanded with more interaction and structure, forming the foundation for future extensions across vessels and mission types.
[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45525680/4494b74de97854fd3eab32765d0bcfb74bcfb6e2.gif"]

The new radio system brings communication to life. You can now contact harbour authorities to request docking, call for towing assistance when needed, and receive event missions directly through radio chatter, making the world feel more connected.
[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45525680/0d81f108071e6df66dfc28c1a8bf31d73a31cf97.png"]

Daily Challenges introduce fresh objectives on a regular basis, encouraging you to return to the sea and take on new tasks. Smaller immersive touches, such as alarm lights during emergency states and cinematic signature scenes when acquiring new vessels, further enhance the atmosphere and presentation of your journey.
As always, this update also includes a wide range of fixes, polish, and quality-of-life improvements.
We’ve also released a new Dev Diary, giving you a closer look at the team and the ongoing development of Seafarer.
[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45525680/3f73ddc1000382ec77cbe55717e311d89849746d.png"]
With Update 3 now released, here’s what’s coming next for Seafarer.

Next up is Early Access Update 4: The Career Update, currently planned for Q2. This update will introduce a “My Career” feature alongside new campaign missions, expanding your long-term progression and goals within the game.
Following that, Update 5 is planned for Q3 and will focus on introducing co-op multiplayer, allowing you to take to the seas together with other players. This update will also introduce new missions.
Looking further ahead, the next phase, our Course to Release, will guide Seafarer toward its full launch, bringing everything together into a complete experience.

As development continues, some updates may be released in phases. This allows us to bring features to you as soon as they’re ready, rather than waiting for a larger release. We've also updated the Early Access Roadmap on Trello: https://trello.com/b/zO1F3oJg/seafarer-the-ship-sim-early-access-roadmap

Our second major Early Access Update for Seafarer: The Ship Sim has officially set sail on the default branch. Thank you to everyone who has already tried out the new features during the Open Beta and left feedback! 🫶
The Rescue Update expands the world of Seafarer with search and rescue gameplay and adds two dedicated rescue vessels to your fleet for this purpose.

notes.title: 🛟 Answer distress calls with the Tide Guard

items.text: With this update, the Tide Guard – Seafarer’s coastguard faction – expands with search and rescue gameplay. Distress calls can come in at any moment, tasking you with locating shipwrecked survivors, assisting people overboard, and transporting them safely back to port.
[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45525680/1bc44a4f9424f85d238c5a17645b57072f1f8d03.gif"]

To aid with search and rescue missions, the Rescue Update adds two dedicated rescue vessels. Salvation serves as the primary search and rescue vessel of the Tide Guard. As one of the most modern and capable coastguard ships in the world of Seafarer, she is built for coordinated emergency response.
Salvation is prepped for the rescue, especially with her daughter boat Grace on board.
[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45525680/385ab2c3a39f361acc317c9c34fb4db490f1ae21.gif"]

Working alongside Salvation is her daughter boat, Grace – a fast and highly maneuverable rescue craft designed to safely approach people in the water. Whether navigating debris fields or reaching survivors in rough conditions, she allows you to get closer, faster – and with greater precision.
Grace is equipped with a rescue net to recover individuals who have fallen into the water.
[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45525680/3a2a710fde267041ae013a141fb9bdcff4b3a66a.gif"]

Search and rescue missions are a core responsibility of the coastguard. And when a distress call comes in, every second matters. Head to the scene of the accident, locate survivors in the water, and act quickly before the sea claims its victims.
Use lifebuoys to stabilize people in the water, or deploy Grace’s rescue net to recover shipwrecked survivors safely and efficiently.
Out there, hesitation can mean the difference between rescue and tragedy – so be ready to respond fast.
The Rescue Update expands Seafarer with additional mission types and a broader range of dynamic events at sea. You may be tasked with transporting fragile or unusual cargo between ports.

Rescue situations can now occur dynamically during your voyages. While navigating the open waters, you might suddenly come across shipwrecked survivors in need of immediate assistance. Every vessel is equipped with lifebuoys, ensuring you’re always prepared to respond when the unexpected happens.
[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45525680/cf2a4ed17b3daee983ec97566eb643b23032bb2a.gif"]

This update introduces the first iteration of our vessel editor, giving you more control over your fleet’s identity. Rename your vessels, add predefined logos, and adjust colors for most ships to create a look that truly represents your company on the water.
[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45525680/9bab61ab30a9b001e8ddcd99436b52cc5a4bbab2.gif"]
Windshield wipers, previously introduced on select vessels, are now also available on Nordic Duchess, Big Trip, and Bulk Willy.

In addition, bow thruster mechanics have been added to Lancer, Nordic Duchess, Big Trip, and Willy, enhancing precision during docking, harbor maneuvers, and other low-speed operations where control matters most.

Alongside the new gameplay features, this update includes numerous bug fixes, performance improvements, balance adjustments, and quality-of-life improvements to further refine the Seafarer experience.

We’re back with our second major Early Access Update – and you can jump in right now to test it!

The Rescue Update introduces search and rescue gameplay, two dedicated rescue vessels, and a range of new missions, events, and improvements. From pulling castaways out of the water to customizing your vessel’s appearance, this update expands life at sea in meaningful new ways.
The update is now available for testing on the public_beta branch. If everything goes smoothly, the full release on the default branch is planned for February 19.
Before we dive into the details, enjoy our small announcement teaser:
[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45525680/f9ff33a697b6b2a159f7a7704ce8f89241300f3c.gif"]

This update expands the Tide Guard, the coastguard faction of Seafarer, with two new vessels and search and rescue gameplay. Whether it’s a distress call nearby or a shipwrecked survivor spotted on the horizon, it’s your job to respond and bring everyone home safely.
[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45525680/1bc44a4f9424f85d238c5a17645b57072f1f8d03.gif"]
⛑️ Meet Salvation

Salvation is a dedicated rescue vessel designed for deployment during emergencies at sea. As one of the largest and most modern coast guard ships in the world of Seafarer, she serves as the primary vessel for search and rescue missions. Recover survivors from the water, provide initial care on board, and transport them safely to the nearest port.
[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45525680/385ab2c3a39f361acc317c9c34fb4db490f1ae21.gif"]

Grace is Salvation’s daughter boat and is designed for speed and precision. Smaller and more maneuverable, she excels at close-range rescue operations, allowing you to approach people in the water where larger ships cannot safely operate.
Together, Salvation and Grace form the backbone of Seafarer’s new rescue gameplay, giving you the tools to respond effectively when distress calls come in.
[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45525680/8c8b62e4320093ac78b6b72cc8663f26378f062a.gif"]

Search and rescue missions are an essential part of coastguard duties. These missions task you with responding quickly to emergencies at sea: head to the scene of the accident, locate and rescue people from the water, provide emergency rations and warm blankets, and safely transport everyone to the nearest port.
And finally, there’s a use for all those lifebuoys on board. 🛟
[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45525680/ffaf4c2d8182d195ea3908ce65438c2dfa65b5e7.gif"]

The Rescue Update not only adds new mission types to the game, but also expands the range of random events you may encounter at sea. Occasionally, you’ll be asked to transport fragile or unusual cargo between ports. Rescue situations can now also appear as random events during your travels at sea. Every ship is equipped with lifebuoys, allowing you to assist shipwrecked people you encounter unexpectedly on your journeys.
[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45525680/cf2a4ed17b3daee983ec97566eb643b23032bb2a.gif"]

[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45525680/9bab61ab30a9b001e8ddcd99436b52cc5a4bbab2.gif"]
With one of our previous updates, we introduced windshield wipers for some vessels. These are now also available on Nordic Duchess, Big Trip, and Bulk Willy.

We’ve also heard your feedback regarding bow thrusters. With this update, thruster mechanics have been added to Lancer, Nordic Duchess, Big Trip and Willy, improving control during docking, harbor navigation, and other low-speed maneuvers.
[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45525680/760a0b4a73e65352bd035adda13bccfbd44495ed.gif"]

Our first major Early Access Update has arrived on the horizon – and you can start testing it right now!

The LNG & Bulk Update, adding new gameplay to the Crescentport Logistics faction, is now available on the ‘public_beta’ branch. If everything goes smoothly, the full release will arrive on the default branch on November 25.
Before we dive into the details, enjoy our announcement teaser:
[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45525680/bd9e2e2721c7280f29b226cfa294da0706e05ded.gif"]
This update expands the cargo side of Seafarer with three new vessels and two new cargo operation types. Let’s take a look at what’s entering the port!
[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45525680/cb6371c18eaf8baf7573309a70b2e5df03ad34e0.gif"]

Big Trip is a giant on the seas – fittingly named the largest container ship in the world of Seafarer. Command its immense deck, handle huge stacks of containers, and experience large-scale container shipping like never before.
[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45525680/9f730fe70a9c5b4cab59763fb72540097839e71a.gif"]
Reliable, sturdy, and a little old-fashioned, Bulk Willy transports unpackaged granulated goods such as building materials like sand.
Explore the rear-mounted bridge tower via its staircase, walk the upper deck, and access the cargo hatches on foot as you learn the ropes of bulk operations.
Nordic Duchess is an LNG tanker; a heavy-duty vessel built for the safe transport of liquefied natural gas. This ship is your entry point into the new LNG gameplay.
[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45525680/64996acf4a47d046bb9e9a6275c06429dfe25151.gif"]
LNG handling is one of the most intricate processes in maritime logistics, and with this update it becomes an immersive new gameplay type in Seafarer.

Once you’ve accepted an LNG transport assignment, it’s time to prepare the ship for loading. LNG tankers use a manifold, a set of hose loading nozzles sealed with flange plugs. Before and after loading, you‘ll need to loosen and retighten the securing bolts on the manifold flange. This opens the connection for fueling and locks it again once the transfer is complete.

At the pier, you’ll guide the shore-based Marine Loading Arm (MLA) into position. After aligning it with the manifold, clamp the systems together and start the LNG transfer. As loading progresses, you’ll monitor the terminal’s pressure controls and keep the system within safe limits.
[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45525680/de911de718b7d2342d79be26f7f00ffb482fb894.gif"]

Bulk Carriers like Willy transport unpackaged materials such as sand. Before loading, open the cargo hatches. At the terminal, a mobile harbor crane with interchangeable attachments is used to fill the holds – and just like in real-life operations, you must never mix different bulk materials within the same hold.
Once loading is complete, simply close the cargo hatches to secure the cargo and prepare the ship for departure.
[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45525680/9bc9c3b90534b64fe3327494d53ae4f9d6af03d4.gif"]
This update also introduces a few new random events on the open seas, adding more variety to your voyages.
You may encounter a ship in distress needing repairs – jump in to assist and get them seaworthy again.
Or you might enjoy a peaceful break with a bit of sightseeing, inviting you to take a photo of a unique landmark or point of interest you discover along your journey.
More events will follow in future updates as we continue expanding life at sea.

Please note that before deleting your files to copy and save them in a secure space!

Since this is a work-in-progress build, there are several issues we are already aware of and working on:
• Multiplayer clients currently do not receive mission rewards after completing a
mission.
• LNG interactions in multiplayer may not update correctly, which can cause pumps to
become stuck until players interact with the controller.
• Using the “Travel To” button in the Job Menu during multiplayer can cause clients to
crash. This appears to occur more frequently over longer travel distances.
• In some situations, players attempting to teleport to another location may instead be
returned to the ship’s deck.
• Bulk Cargo jobs in multiplayer can sometimes not be completed.
Please keep these issues in mind when playing on the Public Beta branch.
